subject: Re: Custom Distribution to Impute Truncated Values

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Custom Distribution to Impute Truncated Values
parts:
Hi Colton,

Thanks for posting the question. The T() syntax only works in model code. nimbleModel will generate the calculations for a truncated distribution based on the declaration using T() syntax. But T() is not a function and thus cannot be called from a nimbleFunction.

I think there is a more fundamental bit to sort out. If you put NA in data in a model and create an MCMC, then an MCMC sampler will be assigned to sample (or impute) values for that node. Therefore, your user-defined distribution dpoisNA will not be called with NA as an argument value.

When you make a user defined distribution as you have, it will be called as
dpoisNA(x = agestart, lambda, agestart).
It won't make sense to have agestart as the random variable (always "x" when called) and also as an argument. Also it looks like your nimbleFunction does not have an argument "x" but does expect something to be called "data", so I wasn't sure what you were trying to have it do.

In case it is helpful and you haven't already been through it, chapter 12 of the User Manual at r-nimble.org covers user-defined distributions.

Can you explain more of what you are trying to do and provide more of a complete example? When you say "impute values", do you mean by MCMC as for missing data, or something else?

Perry


On Fri, Aug 23, 2024 at 8:26 AM Colton Padilla <coltonp...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi everyone,

I am working on creating a model that impute values for unknown ages. To do this, I have a starting and ending age in my data and I randomly assign some of those values as NAs before placing them within the model. I want to create a custom distribution that can impute those values based on a truncated version of that distribution where individuals above a certain age are more likely to be of unknown age. I have thought about it and tried to create a version of it; however, when I tried to register my distribution, I got the error that says "T" must be defined as a nimble function. Could someone help me understand whether or not it is possible to do something the way that I currently have the distribution written out? Thanks for any help in advance.

Here's a small snippet of code and a small model with how I may see this working in practice.

# Custom Poisson
dpoisNA <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(lambda = double(0), age_start = double(1)){
    if(!is.na(data)){
      return(dpois(x, lambda, log = F)/(1 - exp(-lambda)))
    } else{
      return(T(dpois(x, lambda, log = F)/(1 - exp(-lambda)), 212, Inf))
    }
  }
)


#----------------------------#
# Create the nimble model ####
#----------------------------#

# Create a nimble model
sim_code <- nimbleCode({
 
  #---------------------------------#
  # Model to impute unknown ages ####
  #---------------------------------#
 
  # Set a prior for lambda
  lambda ~ dpois(somevalue)
 
  # Model the ages and impute ages that are NA
  agestart ~ dpoisNA(lambda, agestart)

})

Hey Perry,

I am not the best at statistics so I will do my best to describe my issue and how I thought it could be solved originally. I have a situation where females over 4 years old are difficult to age to an exact age. Some of those females will be exactly aged if they die during the study; however, the others we have classified them into a category that just says 4+ as far as age goes. So what I need to do is use the other animals that we have to estimate parameters for an age distribution, while imputing values for those ages from the same distribution but truncated to >= 4 years old. My advisor suggested writing a custom distribution that included some part about 1 - cumulative density function of the distribution and unfortunately he is on travel this week. Here is how I was going to solve this problem originally.

code <- nimbleCode({
 
  # Set prior for distribution
  lambda ~ dpois(value)
 
  # Estimate using the known ages
  ageknown ~ dpois(lambda)
 
  # Imput the unknown values
  ageunknown ~ T(dpois(lambda), 4, Inf)
 
  # Create a derived parameter to use later in the model
  age_full <- c(ageknown, ageunknown)
})

However, my advisor suggested that this may not be the correct way to go about doing this and that writing a custom distribution using the cumulative density function would be the way to go. Sorry if this description is not detailed enough to help with the problem.

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Custom Distribution to Impute Truncated Values
parts:
Hi Colton,
It sounds like it might be a good idea for you to talk more on your end and come back with software questions if that is helpful. I can say a few things from what you've indicated. If you provide ageunknown as data with value NA, then it will be sampled in MCMC, which will impute values for it. It is not clear to me if you want to use a distribution for that age, and if so what distribution. There is also a subtle distinction to make between a truncated distribution and a constraint. You can look up dconstraint in our User Manual to see how to use this trick "distribution" to enforce a constraint. If you want a truncated distribution created with the T() notation for a distribution that you are defining (e.g. T(mydist(param1 ,param2), 4, Inf), then you will need to provide the "q" and "p" functions as well as the "d" function for the distribution. If a user-defined distribution is for an integer random variable (like age), you'll need to register it manually using registerDistributions. These topics should (I hope) be covered in the User Manual section on user-defined distributions.
Perry
